per_depth.common_affordance: The requirement is a balanced 3-partite exact cover: selecting exactly k triples forces exactly one triple per specialist, machine, and time slot, so the search can use compact used-element bitmasks.
The immutable small domain bound k <= 22 makes exponential bitmask/backtracking search appear practical.
The direct reduction of the squad-selection requirement to exact cover over three disjoint resource sets
The task is intrinsically a size-k 3-dimensional matching/exact-cover instance with k <= 22, allowing bitmask search over the three coordinate dimensions.
Because there are exactly k possible x-values, selecting k relays with pairwise distinct x-values is equivalent to selecting one relay from every x-group.
Selecting exactly k relays together with |S_1| × |S_2| × |S_3| = k^3 inherently forces |S_1| = |S_2| = |S_3| = k, i.e. a 3-dimensional matching.
The equality is the unavoidable minimum of three sums of squared counts, so every selected relay must have a distinct value in each coordinate; the problem is therefore 3-dimensional matching.
The binary representation forces each of the three selected coordinate multisets to be exactly {1, 2, ..., k}, turning the problem into a 3-dimensional exact-cover/perfect-matching instance.

per_depth.shortcut_name: one-hot determinants reduce to three-way exact cover
per_depth.common_affordance: The determinant of each one-hot channel matrix is non-zero exactly when the selected relays use every channel value 1..k once, reducing the problem to 3-dimensional matching/exact cover.
